title: listing-messaging-contrasts-and-technical-gatekeeper-notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working log to (1) run rapid copy contrasts for the cloud marketplace listing, and (2) capture the precise technical and compliance gate checks the infra and release teams must sign off on before submission. Goal is to produce 3 small listing copy variants + a clear preflight checklist so we can run marketplace preview + partner review by 2025-02-14.

Background/context:
- Product: Redwood Hosted API (core inference endpoints) with a new Dedicated trial SKU we want in AWS/GCP marketplace first.
- Why separate copy tests: we need both PLG-friendly micro-copy (developer-first) and enterprise-buying path (security/SLA focused). Marketplace listing must reconcile both audiences or offer clear pathing.
- Constraint: legal needs the pricing and trial terms locked before staging push; engineering needs entitlement SKU and metering to be live.

Audience segments (for copy variants):
- Developer-first (DLV): small teams, quick eval, cares about quick start, examples, SDKs, free credits.
- Platform/Infra buyer (INF): procurement/security, cares about SLA, VPC/private deployment, compliance.
- ISV/Partner integrator (ISV): cares about embeddable pricing, multi-tenant quotas, reseller language.

Non-goals:
- Not finalizing pricing in this doc (placeholder numbers only).
- Not describing Dedicated capacity contract terms in full — that's a separate contract doc.

Hypotheses to test:
H1: Developer-first headline that emphasizes "start in 5 minutes" will increase click-to-try by +25% vs enterprise-first headline.
H2: A short compliance badge row (SOC2, ISO27001) visible under the subtitle increases buyer confidence for INF and reduces support questions during trial.
H3: CTA variants where the primary CTA is "Try with free credits" will perform better for DLX; "Contact sales" as primary will convert more leads for INF but reduces trial signups.

Copy variants (short form, usable as marketplace title + subtitle + 3 bullets):
Variant A — Developer (compact)
- Title: "Redwood Inference — Scalable LLM inference, fast SDKs"
- Subtitle: "Start in 5 minutes: sample apps, SDKs, and predictable performance across deployments"
- Bullets: ["One-line REST + SDKs; streaming & function calling","Free credits + example prompts","Auto-batching and cost controls for production"]

Variant B — Enterprise (trust-first)
- Title: "Redwood Inference (Enterprise-ready)"
- Subtitle: "SLA-backed inference with VPC/private deployment and audit logs"
- Bullets: ["Dedicated & private deployment options","Compliance: SOC2 & ISO-ready integrations","Per-route observability and rollout controls"]

Variant C — Partner/ISV hybrid
- Title: "Redwood Inference — For builders & ISVs"
- Subtitle: "Embed inference: flexible metering, SSO, and reseller-friendly licensing"
- Bullets: ["Metered usage + reseller SKUs","Developer quickstart + production toolbelt","Quantization/edge options for cost control"]

CTA experiments (to surface in marketplace metadata):
- CTA1: Try free (primary) / Contact sales (secondary)
- CTA2: Contact sales (primary) / Request trial (secondary)
- CTA3: Start integration (links to GitHub sample) / Contact sales

Micro-copy snippets (for tile + description):
- Short pitch line: "Production-grade LLM serving with predictable latency & costs"
- Price teaser: "Pay-as-you-go + reserved capacity options (contact sales for enterprise pricing)"
- Support blurb: "24/7 support for Dedicated customers; community support for hosted tiers"

Technical preflight & gatekeeper checklist (for engineering + infra sign-off):
- SKU & metering
  - [ ] Marketplace SKU created and mapped to internal product code (MP-SKU-XXXX)
  - [ ] Metering events defined: tokens_generated, requests, embeddings_units
  - [ ] Billing mapping verified with finance (billing team sign-off)
- Entitlement & provisioning
  - [ ] Trial entitlement flow: free credits provisioning end-to-end tested
  - [ ] Dedicated trial provisioning: API + infra templates validated
  - [ ] IAM roles and least-privilege docs included for customer-managed infra
- API & health
  - [ ] Public inference endpoints documented with example requests
  - [ ] Health & readiness endpoints exposed and pass load test (status/ready)
  - [ ] Rate limiting & quota semantics documented (soft vs hard limits)
- Observability & logs
  - [ ] Audit log fields enumerated and sample entries attached
  - [ ] Console dashboard link + sample tracing for a sample request
- Security & compliance
  - [ ] Compliance badges validated vs control owner (SOC2/ISO)
  - [ ] Data handling statement (no retention for hosted by default) reviewed by legal
  - [ ] KMS/HSM integration documented for private deployments
- Packaging & assets for listing
  - [ ] Feature screenshot (console: per-route latency metrics) — 1200x628 px
  - [ ] Architecture diagram (simplified) — SVG + PNG
  - [ ] One-pager PDF (sales-ready) attached
- Trials & activation
  - [ ] Trial length decided (30 days default) and encoded in marketplace metadata
  - [ ] Auto-onboarding flow (sample app + keys) tested end-to-end by QA
- Support & SLAs
  - [ ] Support escalation path included (email + phone for enterprise)
  - [ ] SLA page URL ready and stable
- Legal & contractual
  - [ ] Trial terms and TOU link included in listing copy
  - [ ] Export control checklist for models verified

QA test matrix (minimal):
- Smoke: provisioning + first inference within 3 minutes (pass/fail)
- Load: 10k tokens/sec across 5 concurrent clients (measure latency P50/P95)
- Billing: generate test events and ensure metering pipeline shows event in finance staging
- Security: scan package for secrets and run simple pen test checklist

Marketplace-specific notes / gotchas:
- AWS UI truncates the title at ~80 chars — prefer concise title + subtitle to carry detail.
- Some marketplaces (looking at AWS/GCP) require a separate support contact for public listing vs private offers. Confirm which contact is used per region.
- Screenshots are often used verbatim by listings teams; include minimal sensitive information in images.

Rollout plan & timeline (working):
- 2025-02-03: finalize 3 copy variants and assets (this doc) — owner: Maya
- 2025-02-05: engineering completes SKU + metering (owner: Jon)
- 2025-02-07: legal signs off on trial terms + compliance badges (owner: Aisha)
- 2025-02-10: internal dry run + partner preview (owner: Felix)
- 2025-02-14: submit to marketplace (target)

Acceptance criteria (for submit):
- All checklist items above are checked and have an owner assigned.
- A/B copy variants uploaded to the preview and partner signoff received.
- Trial provisioning successfully exercised by at least 2 partners in preview.

Unresolved questions / decisions to log:
- Q1: Should the listing surface both "Hosted API" and "Dedicated trial" as separate SKUs or a single composite product? (Implication: more approval work vs simpler buyer flow).
- Q2: What exact support contact/email do we list for public marketplace? (Ops or Sales?).
- Q3: Pricing teaser format — USD only or multi-currency?

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- @Felix: can you export a clean console screenshot without customer IDs by 2025-02-04?
- @Aisha: loop in legal control owner for SOC2 badge confirmation.
- Draft the short architecture SVG in the repo under marketplace-samples/assets.

Decision log (append as we go):
- [ ] Decision placeholder: Composite vs separate SKU (owner TBD)

Final thought: keep the listing lean — market wants quick understanding of value + an obvious path to try. The experiment should tell us if we can prioritize developer-first copy on the main tile and surface enterprise trust deeper down (badges + second CTA).

---
This doc is a working surface — feel free to paste copy variants into the comments or push small edits. If something is marked [ ] and you own it, drop a note with the date when complete.
